comment: Pre-registered task suite for the P7 dry-run sweep + the P8 real-robot eval.
Pre-registration: this file is committed BEFORE any eval runs are launched,
so the task set, perturbation magnitudes, and correction scripts cannot be
tuned post-hoc to favour the proposed method. §8.5 paper guideline.
Each task has:
- instruction:       NL goal handed to session.generate(
- corrections:       ordered list of NL corrections applied via session.correct()
(or .correct_with_slate() under SlateGated).
- perturbations:     held-out scene mutations the final program is probed
against to compute the OOD success rate — separate from
the perturbation suite the C2 graduation gate runs.
- early_exit_threshold: OOD pass-rate at which the correction loop terminates,
so corrections_applied is a real measurement of
'corrections-to-success', not the script length.
Pre-registered per task (§8.4).
- success_scorer:    {name, params} for a task-level scorer that gates each
probe on whether the program semantically completed the
task (not just exec-without-crashing). Resolved at
runtime by architect.eval_scorers.build_success_scorer. Without
this the probe runner accepts any non-crashing program
and OOD pass-rate saturates at 100%.
Tuning history:
- schema 1 v1: threshold 0.95, perturbations 10cm/0.785rad. Saturated.
- schema 1 v2: threshold 0.70, perturbations 20cm/1.57rad, +cabinet task.
Still saturated because probes were exec-only.
- schema 1 v3: added success_scorer per task so probes measure pick-place
cycles, not just exec success; replaced side_approach_mug (Claude
inlined, no helpers → library path silent) with stack_three_blocks
(3 cycles forces a helper).
- schema 2 v1 (this commit): the v5 claude sweep showed all conditions
at 100% on pick_place_cycles because the structural close→move→open
scorer accepted programs that closed on empty space. Three coordinated
fixes: (a) pick_place_cycles tightened to require an affirmative
post-grasp get_vqa_response between close and release (default ON;
see architect/eval_scorers.py); (b) new vqa_negative_grasp probe axis
where the first VQA call returns 'no' and the retry returns 'yes',
so verify-once / open-loop programs fail and verify-and-retry
programs recover (see architect/scene_mutator.py); (c) each task's
correction script now includes a verification-demanding step so
the slate's P3 scorer has a target that rewards VQA calls and
the verification candidate has a chance to land as rank-1.

tasks.instruction: Pick up the red block and place it on marker 2. The block must be physically grasped and moved — do not skip the grasp even if the block appears to already be near the marker.
corrections: approach the block from above, not from the side
lift 15 cm after grasping so the block clears any obstacles
after grasping the block, verify with VQA that the gripper is actually holding it; if not, release and retry the grasp

tasks.instruction: Pick up each of the three blocks (red, green, blue) and stack them in a tower with red on the bottom, green in the middle, blue on top. Each block must be picked up and placed in turn — do not skip any block even if it appears already to be in position. The program must execute three complete grasp + place cycles.
corrections: use a small gripper width when grasping so the blocks don't slip
lower carefully when placing — use 1 cm relative descent steps near the contact height
verify each block is placed (e.g., via VQA) before grasping the next

tasks.instruction: Pick up the green block and stack it on top of the red block. The green block must be physically grasped and moved — do not skip the grasp.
corrections: lower more carefully — descend at 5 cm/s near the surface
release the block only after the gripper height stabilises
after grasping the green block, verify with VQA that the grasp succeeded before lifting; if it didn't, release and retry

tasks.instruction: Open the cabinet door, then put the bottle inside, then close the door. Two distinct grasps are required (one for the door handle, one for the bottle) — do not skip either.
corrections: grasp the handle from the side, not from above — the door swings outward on hinges
after opening the door, retract the arm 20 cm before grabbing the bottle so the gripper clears the door edge
place the bottle upright at the back of the cabinet, not at the front lip — leave room for the door to close
after closing the gripper around the bottle, verify with VQA that the grasp is firm before pulling — the bottle is narrow and easy to miss

comment: Progressively harder pick-and-place. Position 0 (pick_block_on_marker)
teaches the agent grasp_at_pose / lift_object. Positions 1-2 reuse those
helpers (under FuncReuse/SlateGated via library retrieval) or re-derive
them (under ICL). This is the cleanest test of the library-compounding
C3 claim — ICL starts from scratch each position; FuncReuse has
registered helpers but none graduated (so retrieval surfaces nothing by
default — retrieval_status='graduated'); SlateGated has graduated
helpers and they appear in later positions' prompts.
Single-position control: cabinet alone. Keeps a non-sequenced cell in the
matrix so we can verify a sequence of length 1 behaves identically to the
old per-task sweep mode.

conditions_comment: Each condition is a boolean toggle on the agentic stack. Flags:
library          - persist Python helpers via write_primitive in library.db
slate            - generate N alternative programs per correction; rank
by probes + scorers + audit; auto-apply or surface
graduation       - probe-test each registered Python helper against K
counterfactual scenes; only promote on pass-rate ≥ 0.7
retrieval        - retrieve top-k relevant Python helpers from library.db
markdown_library - emit + store + retrieve markdown subtask docs at
correction (vs the current LLM-judgment path). Skills
are recomposed into each new program, not literally
inprogram_retry  - generate programs with conditional VQA checks +
one-shot retry per logical step (grasp / place /
articulation). The human is only queried when the
in-program retry budget exhausts AND probes still

ICL.name: In-context learning (no library, no slate, no graduation)

FuncReuse.name: Library of executable Python helpers, retrieval only

SlateGated.name: Slate of alternative programs + counterfactual graduation gate

PatternReuse.name: Single program with in-program VQA retry; markdown subtask doc library
